tagline.text: A traditional-market style shopping complex in Pasig for souvenirs, food and pets

location.label: Location
location.text: Ortigas East, around the corner of Ortigas Avenue and C-5 Road, Ugong, Pasig City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (free entry; based on meals and souvenir shopping)

children.text: Tiendesitas is a shopping complex opened in 2005 on the idea of a traditional Philippine market, with handicraft, fashion, food, furniture and pet shops grouped into themed villages. Entry is free, and it suits souvenir and pasalubong shopping and a light meal.

Tiendesitas takes its name from a Spanish word meaning a collection of little shops. It stands in Ugong, Pasig City, Metro Manila, at the corner where Ortigas Avenue meets C-5 Road, inside Ortigas East, the redevelopment of the former Frontera Verde site. The developer, Ortigas & Company, spent about 200 million pesos on it and opened it on
September 26, 2005

. At the opening, a bonsai exhibit ran for a week, and an antique exhibit followed in October 2005. The complex also has space for trade shows and cultural presentations, and it is said to host such events throughout the year.
Its signature atmosphere is that of a provincial Philippine market moved into the middle of the city. On a site of about

stand twelve pavilions inspired by Maranao architecture, with roofs described as covered in treated cogon grass. More than 450 traders from Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao are said to have stalls here, so you can browse goods from across the country in one place. Some reviewers mention air-conditioned indoor areas that make it comfortable on rainy or hot days, and say it is not very crowded.

The complex is divided into product "villages". The main ones are handicrafts, fashion and accessories, handmade soaps and aromatherapy products, pets, garden plants, antiques, furniture, food, and pasalubong delicacies. You can wander without a plan, or go straight to the village for the item you want. Because several shops selling the same kind of goods sit side by side, it is easy to compare prices and quality, which is a different appeal from a large mall.

Many describe it as closer to a humble traditional market than a glamorous mall. Some reviews say it still feels like a work in progress, while management has said the renovation added parking and dining options, and one review mentions a basement parking area and better restrooms. Facilities and tenants change often, so keep your expectations light. Ortigas East was once part of the Hacienda de Mandaluyon, which was sold in 1920 to Frank W. Dudley and Francisco Ortigas. In 2018 Frontera Verde was renamed Ortigas East and repositioned as a mixed-use estate with about 40% of the land set aside for green and open spaces. Tiendesitas, opened in 2005, was the first facility on this land and has long been the face of the estate.

This is where Philippine-made handicrafts gather. You can compare regional specialty crafts, such as items from Benguet, in one place, which makes it good for choosing gifts for family and friends. Each shop carries different items, so deciding who the gift is for before you walk around saves time.

A food area where about 46 stalls sell regional specialties. It suits travelers who want to take their time tasting Philippine food, and local families come here often too. The menu changes from stall to stall, so a safe approach is to walk a full lap first and pick a stall with a long line or many local customers.
It is described as selling foods such as Vigan empanada and longganisa, Tacloban suman sa latik and Cebu danggit. It is convenient for buying food souvenirs before you fly home.

Licensed pet dealers, pet supply shops and grooming and care services are gathered here. Exotic animals and birds are also mentioned, and reviewers say it is fun even just to look around. Prices and animal condition vary by shop, so be careful before buying. There are also grooming and care services for people who bring their own pets, and some customers come here on purpose just for pet supplies.

Apparel and accessories from Philippine designers and products such as Marikina shoes are mentioned. The personal care area sells handmade soaps, lotions and aromatherapy products, which make good small gifts. Prices differ by shop, so compare before you buy.

The Garden Village sells potted plants, orchids and fruit trees, the Antiques Village has antiques and carvings, and the Furniture Village displays export-quality furniture. They follow one after another, and they are also good for simply looking around rather than buying. Think about storage and shipping before buying large items.
The open pavilion structure inspired by Maranao architecture shapes the feel of the complex. Wikipedia says live entertainment starts every evening at
, but check the current schedule locally.

items.title: Afternoon Shopping Route
items.subtitle: About 2–3 hours of browsing and snacks

children.text: Arrive near the main gate, check where the parking area or the bus interchange is, and take one lap to get a sense of the layout.
Walk through the Handicrafts and Fashion Villages and compare prices. Do not buy right away; look at two or three shops before deciding.
Browse the Garden and Antiques Villages and, for anything you like, ask whether delivery is possible.
Have an early dinner or a snack at the Food Village.
Buy pasalubong food at the Delicacies Village, then head back.

One guide says going in the late afternoon, away from the midday heat, is much more comfortable. Shop hours differ, so finish your rounds before evening. After eating at the Food Village, walk the passages between the villages once more instead of leaving right away, to see shops you missed.

items.title: Pet Browsing Route
items.subtitle: About 1–2 hours around the Pets Village

children.text: Stop by the Pets Village and look over the sales shops, supply shops and grooming and care services.
If you are thinking of buying, ask about the shop's permit and check the animal's health yourself.
Have lunch at the Food Village and head out.
Some individual reviews say certain shops smell or feel expensive, though this is not officially confirmed. Compare what you need at two or three shops.
From central Manila or Makati, a taxi or Grab is the simplest way. Tell the driver "Tiendesitas, Ortigas Avenue corner C-5".
The Ortigas area is very congested during rush hours, so allow plenty of travel time.

Jeepneys and buses along C-5 and Ortigas Avenue are said to reach it. Wikipedia says a bus stop is within walking distance of the gate, and the Ortigas East article says there is a bus interchange at Tiendesitas.
An older review describes taking a jeepney bound for Rosario from Robinsons Galleria and asking the driver to drop you at Tiendesitas. Routes may change, so confirm locally.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), Grab or a taxi is easier when you have luggage. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so leave room in your schedule.
Inside the complex you walk. Many visitors arrive by car, so vehicle entrances and exits can get crowded, and parking spaces are said to surround the complex.
The
November–May
dry season is the most comfortable for walking. Most of the complex is an open pavilion structure, so midday is hot, and passages can get wet on rainy days.

Weekday daytime is said to be the quietest. Weekends and evenings are livelier, with live performances and more diners. One guide recommends going in the late afternoon to enjoy the cooling evening breeze.
Opening hours differ by source, so a fixed daily schedule is hard to give. Check Google Maps or the shops' social media before you go.

The Food Village inside the complex has about 46 stalls, so you can have a meal without looking for a separate restaurant. Which stalls are open now changes over time, so look around when you arrive and then choose.

For lodging, hotels around Ortigas Center and the Megamall area, or on the Pasig and San Juan side, make getting around easier. There are no accommodations in this complex, so see the Ortigas Center guide as well.

When buying food, think separately about what to carry home as pasalubong and what to eat right away. Remembering names such as Vigan empanada and longganisa, Tacloban suman sa latik and Cebu danggit makes them easier to find at the Delicacies Village. For food to eat on the spot, choose a stall that looks hygienic and has a steady flow of customers.

SM Center Pasig, also in Ortigas East, is a supermarket-anchored mall that opened on August 19, 2006. You can use it if you urgently need groceries or daily necessities. Check each business for its operating hours.
Several shops sell similar goods in each village, so do not buy at the first one; compare prices at two or three.
Bring cash. Some shops are said to accept electronic payments, but not all of them do.
For large items or furniture, ask first about delivery and packing.
For food souvenirs before going home, check the expiry date against your departure date, and check your airline's carry-on rules too.
Live performances are said to take place in the evening, but schedules can change, so check on-site announcements.
If you want to buy a pet, check the shop's permit and the animal's health, and look up the quarantine rules of your destination country before taking it abroad.
Going in the late afternoon, away from the midday heat, makes walking easier.
Carry a small, light bag. You will walk a long way holding your purchases, so a large bag is inconvenient.
For items without price tags, politely ask whether bargaining is possible. Some shops have fixed prices, so do not push too hard.
Roads around the complex get very congested on weekends and during evening events. When you call a Grab, decide the exact pickup point in advance.
Opening hours and tenants are described differently by different sources, so check Google Maps or official announcements before visiting.
Online guides give different opening hours (for example 10:00–20:00 and 10:00–22:00), so it is hard to settle on one.
Ortigas East has a long-term redevelopment plan. In 2018 the developer's CEO reportedly said Tiendesitas will stay but be redeveloped in phases, so check the latest news.
Some shops in the Pets Village are said in individual reviews to smell and to be expensive, though this is not officially confirmed. Compare carefully before buying an animal.
As in any ordinary market, watch out for pickpockets and keep valuables in front of you.
The area is congested, so leave extra time before and after your plans.
A large business and shopping district a short drive away, with many hotels and restaurants.
A large mall in Ortigas Center that you can pair with Tiendesitas for a full day of shopping.
A well-known shopping area in San Juan where you can browse souvenirs, jewelry and pearl shops.
A city known for shoemaking, which pairs well with the products at the Fashion Village of Tiendesitas.
A park in Ortigas East that opened in February 2022, described as having picnic areas and pet-friendly spaces.
